questions.q: What caused the duplicate rows in the customer extract?
options: The same export was run twice without clearing the first file, duplicating every (CustomerID, SalesOrderID) pair from the first run
AdventureWorks2012 itself stores duplicate SalesOrderDetail rows
The CASE expression for CustomerSegment produced two rows per customer
Sales.Customer has a broken primary key
questions.explain: A re-run export without clearing the prior output is a realistic, ordinary mistake, not a data corruption issue.

questions.q: What would happen if you summed LineTotal directly on the raw, unduplicated-checked customer extract?
options: Every sale from the first export run would be silently double-counted
The sum would be correct because duplicates cancel out
SQL Server would throw an error automatically
Power BI would refuse to load the file
questions.explain: Duplicate rows inflate any straightforward SUM over LineTotal.

questions.q: What caused the inconsistent TerritoryName values in the territory extract?
options: A spreadsheet review pass introduced inconsistent whitespace and capitalization on some rows
AdventureWorks2012 stores TerritoryName in two different formats natively
The T-SQL extract query had a syntax error
SalesTerritory.Name is a computed column that changes randomly
questions.explain: The inconsistency came from how the extract was handled after the SQL query ran, not from the source table itself.

questions.q: Why would inconsistent TerritoryName text values ('Southwest ' vs 'Southwest') be a real problem later?
options: They can silently break a join or GROUP BY that depends on matching that column by exact text
Power BI automatically trims whitespace, so it's never actually a problem
T-SQL would reject the extract on export
It only affects how the text displays, never any calculation
questions.explain: Text matching for joins and grouping is exact, so whitespace or casing differences cause mismatches.

questions.q: Why does this project clean both issues in Python rather than relying only on manual Power Query clicks?
options: The fixes are short, reviewable code that keeps the whole cross-extract reconciliation in one script, reused for the Lesson 6 join
Power Query is physically incapable of removing duplicate rows
Python is a required step before any CSV can be opened
T-SQL cannot filter on Status = 5 for this data
questions.explain: This is a deliberate skill choice -- pandas keeps the cleaning explicit, reviewable, and reusable for the merge step.
